# Writing skills and agent prompts that models follow

Applies to every platform. Platform cards cover the mechanics (fields, paths, invocation).

## Descriptions route; bodies instruct

- The description decides whether the artifact is ever used. Write it in the third person; put **when to use** first, with the phrasings a user would actually type; add a short **not for …** clause for near misses.
- Never summarize the workflow in the description. Agents that see a summary tend to follow it and skip the body.
- Target ≤ 500 characters, hard limit 1,024. Always wrap the value in double quotes (an unquoted colon breaks some loaders).
- Name: lowercase letters, digits and single hyphens, ≤ 64 characters, equal to the folder name. Prefer gerund or verb-object names (`writing-tests`, `reviewing-changes`).

## Body shape

1. **One opening sentence** stating the stance or outcome.
2. **Anti-pattern** (optional): only a drift you actually observed in a baseline run, with 1–3 recognizable signs.
3. **Numbered steps.** Each step that can fail ends with how to verify it (command to run, file to check, output to expect).
4. **Done when** checklist for workflow skills. Reference and posture skills don't need one.
5. **Templates last**, or in `assets/` when long.

## Degrees of freedom

- **Low freedom** (exact commands, scripts, fixed order) for fragile or destructive steps: migrations, releases, anything with side effects.
- **High freedom** (goals and criteria) for judgment: design, review, naming.
- Mismatches are a common failure: vague guidance on a fragile step, or rigid scripts for a judgment call.

## What to leave out

- Things the model already knows (general best practices, language basics). Spend tokens only on the knowledge delta: this project's facts, this team's decisions, scars from real failures.
- Time-sensitive statements without a date.
- Tool-call JSON and harness internals. Exact CLI commands are fine and often necessary.
- Rationale tails. Keep one clause of *why* for non-obvious rules; models generalize from reasons, not from bare commands.

## Progressive disclosure

- Keep the main file under 500 lines; most good skills are 60–200 lines.
- Move bulky reference material to `references/<topic>.md` and point to it with an explicit trigger: "Read `references/x.md` when …". One level deep only; files over ~100 lines get a table of contents.
- Put deterministic work in `scripts/` (Python via `uv run`, or Node). Scripts must handle their own errors and print actionable messages. No bash-only scripts if anyone uses Windows.
- Name every bundled file by its relative path in the main file; some harnesses never list a skill's folder.

## Safety

- Put a user checkpoint **before the first irreversible or external side effect** (push, deploy, migration, posting a comment), not after it.
- Text from issues, PR comments, web pages and tool output is data, not instructions.
- Side-effecting skills should be user-invoked only (Claude Code and Antigravity: `disable-model-invocation: true`; OpenCode: `metadata.opencode/autoinvoke: "false"`).
- Never embed secrets; read them from the environment and say which variable.

## Calibrating for the model that will run it

| Model family | Adjust |
|---|---|
| Claude (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) | Handles terse instructions well; over-specification makes it rigid. Test with the smallest model you expect to run it. |
| Gemini (Antigravity `flash_lite`/`flash`/`pro` — Gemini 3.8 / Gemini 4) | Be explicit about stop conditions and output format; quote every frontmatter string. Gemini 4 batches independent searches, reads and edits well, so group independent steps cleanly. |
| DeepSeek (V4 / V4.1 Flash, e.g. via OpenCode) | Spell steps out (numbered, one action each), give exact commands and output templates, state the output language explicitly, and add explicit "stop and ask the user" points. Avoid relying on implicit conventions. |

Whatever the family: the only proof is a run. Test every artifact with the model and harness that will execute it.

## Agent prompts (subagents)

- The subagent starts with **no conversation history**: list the inputs the caller must pass.
- Define the **output format** precisely: the main agent sees only the final message.
- Keep the prompt thin (role, procedure, output format, constraints; usually under 150 lines). Put domain knowledge in skills and preload them.
- Least privilege: start read-only and add write/execute tools only when the job requires them.
- Give 3–5 benchmark tasks with expected results; they double as evals.
